intro: A violinist, whistler and loop-pedal architect.
story: Andrew Bird was already a beloved indie violinist, whistler and loop-pedal architect when he played Pickathon in 2013, with records back to 1997. Two Grammy nominations followed, among them Best Folk Album for My Finest Work Yet, and Inside Problems came in 2022. In 2026 he and Gavin Brivik won an Emmy for Need Someone, written for The Pitt, and he played anniversary concerts of The Mysterious Production of Eggs with the Chicago Symphony and Minnesota Orchestra.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 9:20 pm, Woods Stage · Sat Aug 3, 7:20 pm, Mountain View Stage

act: Bradford Lee Folk & The Bluegrass Playboys
intro: A Colorado bluegrass singer with a high, lonesome sound.
story: Bradford Lee Folk is a Colorado bluegrass singer who had fronted Open Road before he brought his band to Pickathon in 2013. In 2025 and 2026 he reunited with Open Road for a run of new singles, among them Rainy Season in September 2026.
sets: Sat Aug 3, 11:10 am, Fir Meadows Stage · Sun Aug 4, 3 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 4, 6:30 pm, Workshop Barn

intro: A Michigan trio of whimsical, cello-laced folk.
story: Breathe Owl Breathe are a Michigan trio of whimsical, cello-laced indie folk who played Pickathon in 2009, 2010, 2011 and again in 2013. Micah Middaugh and his bandmates keep pairing music with visual art, and in December 2026 they announced a winter concert alongside their traveling exhibition Oval Realms.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 11:30 pm, Starlight Stage · Sat Aug 3, 1 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 4, 5:10 pm, Pickathon Cafe

intro: A Northwest duo of sparse, poetic bluegrass.
story: Cahalen Morrison and Eli West are a Northwest duo whose sparse, poetic bluegrass played Pickathon in 2011 and again in 2013. They moved on to solo work and other bands, and in recent years Free Dirt Records pressed their 2012 album Our Lady of the Tall Trees on vinyl for the first time.

intro: A Portland country band, back after 2007.
story: Caleb Klauder had come to Pickathon in 2001 and 2007, and in 2013 he brought his country band. He later formed a duo with Reeb Willms, and the two played Pickathon in 2016 and 2018.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 6:30 pm, Workshop Barn · Sun Aug 4, 8 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A young torchbearer for Louisiana Creole music.
story: Cedric Watson is a fiddler, accordionist and singer from the Louisiana Creole tradition, whose records for the zydeco and Cajun Grammy category drew nominations in 2009, 2010 and 2011, and he brought Bijou Creole to Pickathon in 2013. He and the band remain steady on the road, and played the New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival in April 2026.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 1:50 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sat Aug 3, 9:40 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A Texas honky-tonk traditionalist.
story: Dale Watson is a Texas honky-tonk singer who has recorded since 1990 and who played Pickathon in 2007, 2009 and 2013. He went on to found the Ameripolitan Music Awards, and he remains fiercely independent: Unwanted, self-produced, came out on Forty Below Records, and he keeps an active U.S. tour schedule.
sets: Sat Aug 3, 3 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 4, 4:20 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A supergroup of Spoon and Wolf Parade.
story: Divine Fits paired Britt Daniel of Spoon, Dan Boeckner of Wolf Parade and the drummer Sam Brown, and played Pickathon in 2013 with taut, post-punk swagger, a year after A Thing Called Divine Fits on Merge. The band has been dormant since.
sets: Sat Aug 3, 9:50 pm, Mountain View Stage · Mon Aug 5, late night (1 am), Galaxy Barn

intro: An indie icon whose songs leave space for listening.
story: Feist was already an international indie icon, with Let It Die in 2004, The Reminder in 2007 and Metals in 2011, when she played Pickathon in 2013. She won the Juno for Breakthrough Artist in 2005. Pleasure followed in 2017 and Multitudes in 2023, and in summer 2026 she played outdoor dates at Red Rocks and Brookside Park in Pasadena.
sets: Sat Aug 3, 7:40 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 4, 8:50 pm, Mountain View Stage

intro: A Portland old-time band, here for the sixth time.
story: Foghorn Stringband played Pickathon in 2002, 2003, 2005, 2009, 2010, 2012 and 2013, then again in 2016. They came up as an old-time collective in Portland and became a cornerstone of the stringband revival, still touring internationally, with Northeast dates in 2026.
sets: Sun Aug 4, 3:40 pm, Pickathon Cafe

intro: A theatrical psychedelic duo in a breakout year.
story: Foxygen are Sam France and Jonathan Rado, whose theatrical, 1960s-indebted psychedelic pop made 2013 a whirlwind breakout year, with We Are the 21st Century Ambassadors of Peace & Magic on Jagjaguwar, and they played Pickathon that summer. ...And Star Power followed in 2014 and Hang in 2017. The duo stepped back from touring after Seeing Other People in 2019.
sets: Sat Aug 3, 6:20 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 4, 2:50 pm, Fir Meadows Stage

intro: A towering voice in traditional Appalachian singing.
story: Ginny Hawker is a ballad singer from the Appalachian tradition who came to Pickathon in 2013 with her husband and harmony partner Tracy Schwarz, as a towering voice in traditional singing. Tracy Schwarz died on March 29, 2025, at 86.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 3 pm, Galaxy Barn · Fri Aug 2, 5:10 pm, Pickathon Cafe · Sat Aug 3, 5 pm, Workshop Barn

intro: The Tucson desert-rock godfather.
story: Howe Gelb led Giant Sand for decades out of Tucson and brought his dusty, off-the-cuff Americana to Pickathon in 2013, two years before the band came to the farm. Fire Records pressed his 2001 album Confluence on vinyl for the first time.
sets: Sat Aug 3, 2:40 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 4, 12:30 pm, Workshop Barn · Sun Aug 4, 11:30 pm, Starlight Stage

intro: A Dublin band of Irish storytelling and string-band drive.
story: I Draw Slow are a Dublin quintet who brought Irish storytelling and Appalachian string-band drive to Pickathon in 2013 as rising transatlantic favorites, and they returned in 2016. Led by the siblings Dave and Louise Holden, they still tour internationally.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 3:40 pm, Pickathon Cafe · Sat Aug 3, 6:30 pm, Workshop Barn · Mon Aug 5, late night (1 am), Starlight Stage

intro: An Oklahoma singer of crisp, vintage rock and roll.
story: JD McPherson is an Oklahoma singer and guitarist whose crisp rock-and-roll and R&B drew an Americana Music Association emerging-act nomination in 2013, the year he came to Pickathon. He returned in 2015, with Let the Good Times Roll. In March 2026 he scored the film The Lowdown, and in December 2026 he toured with Melissa Carper, with stops at Portland's Aladdin Theater and Seattle's Tractor Tavern.
sets: Sat Aug 3, late night (1 am), Galaxy Barn · Sat Aug 3, 8:40 pm, Fir Meadows Stage

intro: A Portland bluegrass band, here for the sixth time.
story: Jackstraw are a Portland bluegrass quartet, known since 1994 for their gritty, honky-tonk-inflected sound, who played Pickathon in 2001, 2003, 2005, 2007, 2009 and 2013, and again in 2022. They have stayed loyal to home, and recently played a Portland FolkMusic Society show.

intro: A solo guitarist with an otherworldly voice.
story: Jessica Pratt came to Pickathon in 2013, a year after her self-titled debut on Birth Records, with only an acoustic guitar and a mysterious, otherworldly voice. She returned in 2015, with On Your Own Love Again on Drag City. Quiet Signs followed in 2019 and Here in the Pitch in 2024, widely praised, and in summer 2025 she played festivals in Europe and California.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 2:40 pm, Woods Stage · Sat Aug 3, 3:30 pm, Workshop Barn

intro: Kyle Thomas's fuzzy glam-garage anthems.
story: King Tuff is Kyle Thomas, whose fuzzy, hook-filled glam-garage anthems came to Pickathon in 2013, a year after his self-titled album on Sub Pop. Black Moon Spell followed in 2014 and he returned in 2015. The Other came in 2018 and Smalltown Stardust in 2023, in gentler psych-folk textures. In late 2026 he played club dates with Sheer Mag.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 11:20 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sat Aug 3, 2:40 pm, Mountain View Stage

intro: A Philadelphia guitarist of languid, fingerpicked epics.
story: Kurt Vile brought his languid, fingerpicked guitar epics to Pickathon in 2013, the year of Wakin on a Pretty Daze on Matador, after Smoke Ring for My Halo in 2011. b'lieve i'm goin down came in 2015, Bottle It In in 2018 and (watch my moves) in 2022. Philadelphia's been good to me arrived on Verve in May 2026, and he toured the U.S. that November.
sets: Sat Aug 3, 11 pm, Starlight Stage · Sun Aug 4, 6:20 pm, Mountain View Stage

intro: A soul duo of Nicole Wray and Terri Walker.
story: Lady were Nicole Wray and Terri Walker, a soul duo whose rich, retro harmonies came to Pickathon in 2013 around their one self-titled album. The duo was a one-off, and Wray carried on as Lady Wray, with Cover Girl in 2025 and Cover Girl (Instrumentals) in May 2026.
sets: Sat Aug 3, 5 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sun Aug 4, 11:20 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A scrappy conservatory-bred band, back after 2012.
story: Lake Street Dive were a scrappy, conservatory-bred quartet winning crowds one set at a time when they played Pickathon in 2012, and they returned in 2013. The Americana Music Association nominated them for Duo/Group of the Year in 2014 and 2016. Side Pony came in 2016, Obviously in 2021 and Good Together in 2024, and What About Flamingos? is due in February 2027.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 6 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 4, 2 pm, Pickathon Cafe · Sun Aug 4, 6:20 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A Texas honky-tonk songwriter of plainspoken storytelling.
story: Leo Rondeau is a Texas honky-tonk singer-songwriter whose plainspoken country storytelling came to Pickathon in 2013. He is rooted in Austin's dancehall scene, and in November 2026 he played The White Horse there with Sentimental Family Band and Kristina Murray.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 3 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Sun Aug 4, 1:20 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: Moody synth-rock from the Black Mountain family.
story: Lightning Dust is a Vancouver duo of Amber Webber and Joshua Wells, a moody synth-rock side project of Black Mountain, who played Pickathon in 2011 and again in 2013, the year of Fantasy on Jagjaguwar. They have recorded only sporadically since.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 7:40 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Sun Aug 4, 6 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A North Carolina troubadour of gravelly folk-blues.
story: Malcolm Holcombe was a North Carolina songwriter whose gravelly, fiercely honest folk-blues had been recorded since 1994, and he played Pickathon in 2013. He died in 2024, and Jason Isbell and Lucinda Williams are among those who remember him.
sets: Sat Aug 3, 2 pm, Workshop Barn · Sun Aug 4, 11:40 am, Galaxy Barn

intro: A keyboardist of groove-heavy piano experiments.
story: Marco Benevento brought joyful, groove-heavy piano experiments to Pickathon in 2013, and returned in 2014. He is now a fixture of the Hudson Valley scene, and released Glera on Big Crown in 2026 and hosted the fifth year of his Follow the Arrow Festival.
sets: Sat Aug 3, late night (1 am), Starlight Stage · Sun Aug 4, 9:20 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A Portland band of gritty harmonies.
story: Old Light are a Portland band of gritty Americana and multipart harmonies who played Pickathon in 2011 and again in 2013, after a KEXP session and Northwest dates.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 6:20 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 4, 12:30 pm, Fir Meadows Stage

intro: A deadpan post-punk band as their breakout accelerated.
story: Parquet Courts tore through Pickathon in 2013 with wired, deadpan post-punk energy, a year after Light Up Gold, just as their indie breakout accelerated, and they came back in 2014. Human Performance, in 2016, had packaging nominated for a Grammy, and Wide Awake! followed in 2018 and Sympathy for Life in 2021. Andrew Savage's new band, Iconic Fugues, announced 2027 European dates.
sets: Sun Aug 4, late night (1 am), Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 4, 7:40 pm, Fir Meadows Stage

intro: British Columbia banjo makers and harmony singers.
story: Pharis and Jason Romero are British Columbia banjo makers and harmony singers whose warm old-time acoustics came to Pickathon in 2013. They still craft instruments and songs from their rural workshop, and released These Are the Days That Turn into Years in 2026.
sets: Sun Aug 4, 1 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A Portland dream-pop duo.
story: Pure Bathing Culture are a Portland dream-pop duo of Sarah Versprille and Daniel Hindman, who played Pickathon in 2013, around their debut, Moon Tides, on Partisan. Pray for Rain followed in 2015, and in November 2025 they released the single I Said What I Said on Father/Daughter Records.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 12:40 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Fri Aug 2, 4:40 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A Portland rockabilly-tinged band.
story: Sallie Ford led The Sound Outside through brassy, vintage rock in Portland, and they played Pickathon in 2010 and 2013 before parting ways in 2014. Ford has since made solo albums, including Soul Sick on Vanguard in 2017.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 6:30 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sun Aug 4, 4:40 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: Ishmael Butler's cosmic Seattle hip-hop.
story: Shabazz Palaces are Ishmael Butler's Seattle collective, whose cosmic, boundary-pushing hip-hop came to Pickathon in 2013, two years after Black Up on Sub Pop, and they returned in 2015. Lese Majesty followed in 2014. Their eighth album, It's A Style Sport, came out on Sub Pop in October 2026.
sets: Sat Aug 3, 8 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 4, 7:40 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A scrappy Austin one-man band with a suitcase drum.
story: Shakey Graves is Alejandro Rose-Garcia, a scrappy Austin one-man band who kicked a suitcase drum and howled folk-blues when he came to Pickathon in 2013. The Americana Music Association named him Emerging Act of the Year in 2015, and And the War Came was nominated for Album of the Year. He returned in 2014, 2018 and 2026, and in 2026 released Fondness, Etc.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 5 pm, Workshop Barn · Sat Aug 3, 5:10 pm, Pickathon Cafe · Sun Aug 4, 10 pm, Starlight Stage

intro: A confessional songwriter becoming a defining voice.
story: Sharon Van Etten brought raw, confessional folk-rock to Pickathon in 2013, the year after Tramp on Jagjaguwar, as her voice became a defining force in indie music. Are We There followed in 2014, Remind Me Tomorrow in 2019 and We've Been Going About This All Wrong in 2022. Sharon Van Etten & the Attachment Theory came in February 2025, and she finished a year-long world tour.
sets: Sat Aug 3, 4:20 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 4, 4 pm, Mountain View Stage

intro: Kevin Russell's horn-fueled Austin soul and swamp-pop.
story: Shinyribs began as a side project of Kevin Russell of The Gourds when he played Pickathon in 2007, and he returned in 2008, 2013 and 2018. It has grown into his full-time, horn-fueled Austin institution, and played a full slate of Texas dates, among them the Fort Worth Songwriter's Festival.
sets: Sat Aug 3, 11:20 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 4, 11:20 am, Mountain View Stage

intro: A fiercely independent honky-tonk singer, just beginning to shake up country.
story: Sturgill Simpson played Pickathon in 2013, the year before Metamodern Sounds in Country Music, and in 2014 the Americana Music Association named him Emerging Act of the Year. A Sailor's Guide to Earth, in 2016, won the Grammy for Best Country Album. He has kept reinventing himself: Cuttin' Grass in 2020, and in March 2026 Mutiny After Midnight as Johnny Blue Skies & the Dark Clouds, with a tour.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 4:20 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A Portland band of percussive banjo folk-rock.
story: The Builders and the Butchers formed on Portland's streets and played Pickathon in 2011 and again in 2013 with percussive, banjo-driven folk-rock. With members scattered across the country, they reconvened to release No Tomorrow on Badman Recording Co.
sets: Sun Aug 4, 2:50 pm, Fir Meadows Stage

intro: Brothers with Everly-style blood harmonies.
story: The Cactus Blossoms are the brothers Jack Torrey and Page Burkum, whose Everly-style blood harmonies were a Midwestern secret when they played Pickathon in 2012, and they returned in 2013 and again in 2025. You're Dreaming came on Red House in 2016, and they had a cameo on Twin Peaks. They toured the Southwest and California in late 2026.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 1 pm, Woods Stage · Sat Aug 3, 2 pm, Pickathon Cafe · Sun Aug 4, 2 pm, Workshop Barn

intro: A Santa Cruz string-band punk trio.
story: The Devil Makes Three are a Santa Cruz trio of rowdy, ragtime-inflected string-band punk who came to Pickathon in 2013, the year of I'm a Stranger Here on New West, and the Americana Association nominated them for Duo/Group of the Year in 2014. Redemption & Ruin followed in 2016 and Spirits in 2025, and in 2026 they played Bourbon & Beyond, Grand Targhee and the Holland Blues Festival.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 8:50 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sat Aug 3, 9:20 pm, Woods Stage

intro: Ragged, literary Catskills folk-rock.
story: The Felice Brothers are a Catskills folk-rock band of accordions, fiddles and Dylan-esque storytelling who played Pickathon in 2013, after Celebration, Florida on Fat Possum. Life in the Dark came on Yep Roc in 2016 and From Dreams to Dust in 2021. In summer 2026 they toured Europe and North America, with Newport Folk Festival and U.K. dates.
sets: Sun Aug 4, late night (12:30 am), Starlight Stage · Sun Aug 4, 5:10 pm, Fir Meadows Stage

intro: A Brooklyn trio of soaring three-part harmonies.
story: The Lone Bellow are a Brooklyn-formed trio with Zach Williams who came to Pickathon in 2013, just after their self-titled debut on Descendant Records. Then Came the Morning followed in 2015, with an Americana Duo/Group of the Year nomination. They are still on the road, with U.S. dates through November 2026 and into early 2027.
sets: Sat Aug 3, 6:10 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Sun Aug 4, 2:40 pm, Woods Stage

intro: Dallas gospel-funk pioneers, rediscovered.
story: The Relatives are a Dallas psychedelic gospel-funk group whose 1970s recordings were rediscovered, and they brought revival-tent energy to Pickathon in 2013. The Living Blues critics had named them an artist deserving more attention in 2011. The Numero Group released the archival album Don't Let Me Fall in January 2025.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 9:40 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sat Aug 3, 12:20 pm, Mountain View Stage

intro: A North Carolina songwriter of soulful country-folk.
story: Tift Merritt is a North Carolina songwriter whose warm, soulful country-folk played Pickathon in 2013. Her album Tambourine was nominated for a Grammy and for the Americana Music Association's Album of the Year, and Stitch of the World followed on Yep Roc in 2017. In 2025 and 2026 she opened her vaults with kitchen sessions and catalog reissues.
sets: Sat Aug 3, 1:20 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 4, 1:40 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sun Aug 4, 5 pm, Workshop Barn

intro: A garage-rock dynamo, here for the first of four visits.
story: Ty Segall brought high-volume fuzz and relentless energy to Pickathon in 2013 as a young DIY standard-bearer, and returned in 2015, 2016 and 2017. He has kept recording steadily: Freedom's Goblin in 2018, Possession in 2025 and Chrome in 2026, with the companion EP Love Fuzzz and a South American tour in November.
sets: Sat Aug 3, 6 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 4, 9:40 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A Malian guitarist of desert blues.
story: Vieux Farka Toure is a Malian guitarist whose dazzling desert blues carries on the legacy of his father, Ali Farka Toure, and he came to Pickathon in 2013, after Fondo in 2009. In 2022 he made a collaboration with Khruangbin, and he came back to the farm in 2023.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 7:40 pm, Woods Stage · Sat Aug 3, 3:50 pm, Fir Meadows Stage

intro: A Texas king of juke-joint swing.
story: Wayne Hancock was an undisputed king of juke-joint swing and a Texas honky-tonk traditionalist who had played Pickathon in 2008 and returned in 2013. He kept up a relentless road schedule for decades, and there is no recent news.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 8 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sat Aug 3, 1:30 pm, Fir Meadows Stage

intro: Tim Presley's lo-fi garage-psych.
story: White Fence is Tim Presley's lo-fi garage-psych project, a cult favorite when it played Pickathon in 2013, after Family Perfume Vol. 1 and Vol. 2 in 2012 on Woodsist. Presley stepped back to paint, and in 2026 returned with Orange, the first White Fence album in seven years, on Drag City.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 5:20 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Sat Aug 3, 4:40 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: Sam Cohen's psychedelic pop project.
story: Yellowbirds was Sam Cohen's psychedelic pop project, which came to Pickathon in 2013 around its second album, Songs from the Vanished Frontier. The band wrapped up in 2014. Cohen came back to the farm in 2015.
sets: Fri Aug 2, 4:10 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sat Aug 3, 11:40 am, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 4, 3:30 pm, Workshop Barn
